knowledge_tree.title: PEP Primary English Grade 6 Book 1
knowledge_tree.content: English textbook for Grade 6 students (3rd grade starter), covering topics like places, transportation, weekend plans, hobbies, jobs, and emotions.

children.title: Unit 1: How can I get there?
children.content: Asking for and giving directions to places in a city/town.

children.title: Places vocabulary
children.content: Names of common places: science museum, post office, bookstore, cinema, hospital, pet hospital, park, library, zoo, school.

children.title: Prepositions of place
children.content: Words to describe location: near, next to, beside, behind, in front of, over there.

children.title: Asking for directions
children.content: Question patterns: 'Where is the...?', 'How can I get to the...?', 'Is there a...?'

children.title: Giving directions
children.content: Using imperative sentences: 'Turn left/right at...', 'Go straight', 'It's next to/near...'

children.title: Reading a map
children.content: Understanding and following directions on a simple map.

children.title: Unit 2: Ways to go to school
children.content: Talking about different modes of transportation and traffic safety.

children.title: Transportation vocabulary
children.content: Modes of transport: on foot, by bus, by plane, by taxi, by ship, by subway, by train, by sled, by ferry.

children.title: Frequency adverbs
children.content: Words describing how often: usually, often, sometimes.

children.title: Traffic safety rules
children.content: Understanding and following traffic rules: stop at red light, go at green light, slow down at yellow light, wear a helmet, pay attention to traffic lights.

children.title: Comparative transportation
children.content: Comparing how people go to school in different countries/cultures.

children.title: Unit 3: My weekend plan
children.content: Talking about future plans using 'be going to' structure.

children.title: Future time expressions
children.content: Words indicating future time: this morning/afternoon/evening, tonight, tomorrow, next week.

children.title: Activities vocabulary
children.content: Common weekend activities: visit grandparents, go to the supermarket, see a film, take a trip, go ice-skating, wash clothes, draw pictures, make a snowman, go for a picnic.

children.title: 'Be going to' structure
children.content: Using 'be going to' to talk about future plans: 'I'm going to...', 'What are you going to do?'

children.title: Asking about plans
children.content: Question patterns: 'What are you going to do?', 'Where are you going?', 'When are you going?'

children.title: Unit 4: I have a pen pal
children.content: Talking about hobbies and corresponding question forms.

children.title: Hobbies vocabulary
children.content: Common hobbies: dancing, singing, reading stories, playing football, doing kung fu, doing word puzzles, going hiking, studying Chinese, cooking Chinese food.

children.title: Asking about hobbies
children.content: Question patterns: 'What are your hobbies?', 'What are Peter's hobbies?'

children.title: Simple present tense
children.content: Using simple present to describe regular activities: 'He likes...', 'She lives...'

children.title: Yes/No questions with 'does'
children.content: Asking and answering questions: 'Does he live in Sydney?', 'Does he like doing word puzzles?'

children.title: Unit 5: What does he do?
children.content: Talking about different jobs and workplaces.

children.title: Jobs vocabulary
children.content: Common occupations: factory worker, postman, businessman, police officer, fisherman, scientist, pilot, coach, head teacher, doctor, secretary, sports reporter, PE teacher.

children.title: Workplaces vocabulary
children.content: Places where people work: sea, university, gym, office, pet hospital, rescue plane.

children.title: Asking about occupations
children.content: Question patterns: 'What does he do?', 'Where does he work?', 'How does he go to work?'

children.title: Future career aspirations
children.content: Talking about what you want to be: 'I want to be a...', 'I'm going to be a...'

children.title: Unit 6: How do you feel?
children.content: Expressing emotions and giving advice.

children.title: Emotions vocabulary
children.content: Words describing feelings: angry, afraid, sad, worried, happy, ill, cold.

children.title: Giving advice
children.content: Using 'should' to give suggestions: 'You should see a doctor', 'You should take a deep breath'

children.title: Asking about feelings
children.content: Question patterns: 'How do you feel?', 'What's wrong?'

children.title: Health and wellness
children.content: Talking about being healthy: 'stay healthy', 'do more exercise', 'wear warm clothes'

children.title: Recycle 1 & 2
children.content: Review units consolidating previous learning.

children.title: Integrated language use
children.content: Applying learned language in new contexts and stories.

children.title: Story comprehension
children.content: Understanding and retelling simple stories in English.

children.title: Language Focus Areas
children.content: Key grammatical structures and language patterns

children.title: Question forms
children.content: Wh-questions and Yes/No questions in different tenses.

children.title: Tenses
children.content: Simple present, present continuous, and 'be going to' for future.

children.title: Modal verbs
children.content: Using 'can', 'should', 'must' for ability, advice, and obligation.
